name: Kettlebell Offset Rack Squat
description: A squat with the kettlebell racked on ONE side only. The single-side (offset) load pulls the torso toward the loaded side, so the core has to fight lateral flexion and rotation the whole way down and up — far more trunk demand than a symmetric goblet or double-rack front squat. Feet shoulder-width, sit into the squat with the chest tall and the racked elbow up, resist the pull, drive up through the whole foot. A low-load, high-stability squat variant that trains the legs and the anti-lateral-flexion core together.
